Class DefaultHttpRouteBuilder

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.web.router.builder.DefaultHttpRouteBuilder
All Implemented Interfaces:
HttpRouteBuilder, HttpRouteScope
@Internal public final class DefaultHttpRouteBuilder extends Object implements HttpRouteBuilder
The HttpRouteBuilder: adds the routes to handler functions to a RouteAssembly, like the legacy route builder adds its routes, without depending on it. It has no route filter methods: it is shared by the HttpRoutes beans, and a group, see group(Consumer), is the scope of route filters.
Since:
5.3.0
Author:
Denis Stepanov

    • group

      public void group(Consumer<HttpRouteGroup> routes)
      Description copied from interface: HttpRouteBuilder
      Declare a group of routes, whose filters apply to every route declared in the lambda, e.g. to filter every route of an HttpRoutes bean. The builder of an HttpRoutes bean has no route filter methods of its own, as it is shared by the beans: the group is the scope of the filters, see HttpRouteBuilder.serverFilter(String...) for a server filter. 
      routes.group(all -> {
    all.beforeReplacing((request, propagatedContext) -> {
        propagatedContext.add(new MdcPropagationContext(Map.of("path", request.getPath())));
        return null;
    });
    all.GET("/orders", ordersHandler);
    all.GET("/customers", customersHandler);
});

      See HttpRouteGroup for which routes the filters apply to, and in which order. A route declared in the lambda is ended with a terminal, see HttpRouteSpec, before the lambda returns: otherwise the group fails with an IllegalStateException naming the route.

      Specified by:
      group in interface HttpRouteBuilder
      Parameters:
      routes - Declares the routes and the filters of the group

    • path

      public void path(String prefix, Consumer<HttpRouteGroup> routes)
      Description copied from interface: HttpRouteBuilder
      Declare a group of routes under a prefix: the URI template of every route of the group, including the routes of its nested groups, is the prefix followed by the URI template of the route, like the URI of a controller method under the URI of the controller: path("/api", api -> api.GET("/orders", handler)) routes GET /api/orders. The prefixes of nested groups add up. The filters of the group apply to every route declared in the lambda, see HttpRouteGroup.

      The prefix is a path: it may have path variables, e.g. /tenants/{tenant}, but no query or fragment.

      Specified by:
      path in interface HttpRouteBuilder
      Parameters:
      prefix - The prefix of the URI templates of the routes of the group
      routes - Declares the routes and the filters of the group

    • serverFilter

      public ServerFilterSpec serverFilter(String... patterns)
      Description copied from interface: HttpRouteBuilder
      Declare a server filter, the functional form of a @ServerFilter bean: it filters every request whose path matches one of the patterns, e.g. /** or /api/**, whatever answers it, a controller, a handler route or a static resource, including the requests no route matches, ordered together with the filter beans. It is global: only the builder of an HttpRoutes bean declares server filters, a HttpRouteGroup declares route filters, which apply to its routes only. 
      routes.serverFilter("/**").order(100).beforeReplacing((request, propagatedContext) -> {
    propagatedContext.add(new MdcPropagationContext(Map.of("path", request.getPath())));
    return null;
});

      Each call declares a new server filter. The server filters of an HttpRoutes bean are read when the router is built.

      Specified by:
      serverFilter in interface HttpRouteBuilder
      Parameters:
      patterns - The patterns of the paths to filter, in the style of the filter, ANT by default
      Returns:
      The server filter, to declare its filters on

      public HttpRouteSpec route(HttpMethod method, String uri)
      Description copied from interface: HttpRouteScope
      Declare a route of the requests of a method. The route runs like a controller method: filters, error routes, body readers and writers and executor selection apply as they do for a controller method. Like a controller route it consumes JSON unless RouteSpec.consumes(MediaType...) says otherwise, and in HttpRoutes its URI is under micronaut.server.context-path. A GET route gets an implicit HEAD route.

    • any

      public HttpRouteSpec any(String uri)
      Description copied from interface: HttpRouteScope
      Declare the routes of the requests of any HTTP method, standard or custom, to one handler: a route per standard method and one for the custom methods, which the pending route configures together.
      • A route of a specific method that matches a request as closely as the route of any method, e.g. GET on the same path, answers the request instead: the route of any method answers the other methods.
      • The implicit HEAD route of a GET route on the same path answers a HEAD request before it, and a CORS preflight request is answered by the CORS filter as before: the route of any method answers the other OPTIONS and HEAD requests.
      • A path the route matches is never answered with 405: every method has a route. A more specific route of another method on a path the route matches does not change that.
      Specified by:
      any in interface HttpRouteScope
      Parameters:
      uri - The URI template
      Returns:
      The pending routes, to configure together
      See Also:
      • HttpRouteScope.route(Set, String)

    • error

      public final <E extends Throwable> ErrorRouteSpec error(Class<E> type, ErrorRouteHandler<E> handler)
      Description copied from interface: HttpRouteScope
      Handle the exceptions of a type, and of its subtypes, with a handler function. Where it is declared decides which routes it answers for:
      • declared on the builder of an HttpRoutes bean, it is global, like an @Error(global = true) method: it answers requests to controller routes and handler routes that fail with such an exception;
      • declared in a group, it is local to the routes of the group and of its nested groups, like an @Error method of a controller is local to the routes of the controller.
      routes.error(NoSuchFileException.class, (request, error) -> HttpResponse.notFound()); // global
routes.path("/api", api -> {
    api.error(IllegalArgumentException.class, (request, error) -> HttpResponse.badRequest(error.getMessage())); // /api routes only
    api.GET("/orders/{id}", ordersHandler);
});

      The error route of a failed handler route is looked up in its innermost group first, then in the groups around it, then among the global error routes, the error routes of controllers and of HttpRoutes beans; within each level, the error route of the closest exception type answers. So a group's error route for a supertype wins over a global error route for the exact type, like the local error route of a controller does. A route that implements a bean method, see RouteSpec.annotationMetadata(AnnotationMetadataProvider), first has the local error routes of the bean class. An error of a request no route matched, e.g. a 404 or a 405, is answered by the global error routes only.

      Specified by:
      error in interface HttpRouteScope
      Type Parameters:
      E - The type of the exception
      Parameters:
      type - The type of the exception
      handler - The handler
      Returns:
      The error route

    • status

      public final StatusRouteSpec status(HttpStatus status, StatusRouteHandler handler)
      Description copied from interface: HttpRouteScope
      Handle the responses of a status with a handler function, e.g. to answer 404. Declared on the builder of an HttpRoutes bean, it is global, like an @Error(status = ..., global = true) method; declared in a group, it is local to the routes of the group, like an @Error(status = ...) method of a controller: it answers the responses of that status that a route of the group produces, or an HttpStatusException of that status a route of the group throws, see HttpRouteScope.error(Class, ErrorRouteHandler) for the order of the lookup. A request under the prefix of a group that no route matches, a 404, is answered by the global status routes only, as no route of the group matched it.
      Specified by:

      status - The status

    • locate

      public final <T> void locate(String prefixUri, LocatorHandler<? extends T> locator, Function<? super T, ? extends LocatedRoutes<?>> routesOf)
      Description copied from interface: HttpRouteScope
      Route the requests under a prefix to the routes of a target located at runtime, like a JAX-RS sub-resource locator. The prefix, e.g. /orders/{id}, is matched for every standard HTTP method, followed by the rest of the path, which is empty or starts with a slash. When the router selects the locator route, it runs the locator, and matches the rest of the path, e.g. /items/3 of /orders/5/items/3, with the LocatedRoutes of the target: the request is handled by the route they declare, as if they were the application routes, with the path variables of the prefix and of the route, and with the target, see LocatedRoutes.locatedTarget(PathVariables). A locator route of the located routes locates again, from the rest of the path. 
      routes.locate("/orders/{id}",
    (request, pathVariables) -> orders.find(pathVariables.getLong("id")),
    order -> order.isArchived() ? archivedOrderRoutes : orderRoutes);

      The type of the target is the type the locator returns: the function receives it, e.g. to choose the routes of a subtype. The handlers of the located routes receive the target of the type of the routes, see LocatedRoutes.targetType(); a located target that is not an instance of that type fails the request, answered by the error routes like a failed controller method.

      When the located routes have no route for the rest of the path, the request is answered like a request that no route matches: 404, or 405, 415 or 406 if a located route matches the path with another method or media type. No other route of the application is tried. The filters of the matched located route apply, after the filters of the groups of the locator route, and the server filters apply to the full path. A located route inherits the annotations, the attributes, the media types and the executor of the groups of the locator route, like a route declared in them, unless it, or a group of its LocatedRoutes, declares its own, see HttpRouteGroup.

      The locator runs while the request is matched, see LocatorHandler, at most once per request: matching the request again, e.g. to find the allowed methods of a 405, reuses the target, or the exception, of the first call. The routes of a LocatedRoutes instance are declared once, when the first target it routes is located, and shared by every locator that returns the instance; routes that fail to declare, e.g. a global error route, fail every request routed to them, and are declared again for the next one. The prefix is a path, without a query or a fragment. A request with a custom HTTP method is located like any other: the located routes of that method answer it, or those declared with any(...), and the allowed methods of its 405 are those of the located routes.

      Specified by:
      locate in interface HttpRouteScope
      Type Parameters:
      T - The type of the target
      Parameters:
      prefixUri - The URI template of the prefix
      locator - Locates the target, or answers null for 404
      routesOf - The routes of a located target

    • locateAsync

      public final <T> void locateAsync(String prefixUri, AsyncLocatorHandler<? extends T> locator, Function<? super T, ? extends LocatedRoutes<?>> routesOf)
      Description copied from interface: HttpRouteScope
      Route the requests under a prefix to the routes of a target located asynchronously, e.g. loaded from a database: the same as HttpRouteScope.locate(String, LocatorHandler, Function), but the locator returns a stage of the target, and the router matches the rest of the path with the routes of the target when the stage completes, without blocking the thread that matches the request. See AsyncLocatorHandler. 
      routes.locateAsync("/orders/{id}",
    (request, pathVariables) -> orders.findAsync(pathVariables.getLong("id")), // completes with null: 404
    order -> orderRoutes);

      The filters of the located route, the error routes and the server filters apply like for HttpRouteScope.locate(String, LocatorHandler, Function); the located routes may locate again, synchronously or asynchronously. The target is located once per request. Router.findClosest(HttpRequest) of an application with an asynchronous locator that has not located its target yet fails: the server matches such a request again when the stage completes. A server that tells when the client goes away, e.g. closes the connection or resets the HTTP/2 stream, stops waiting for the stage then, without cancelling it: a locator may return a stage it shares with other requests, e.g. of a cache. A CORS preflight request of the prefix is answered once the target is located, with the methods of its routes.

      Specified by:
      locateAsync in interface HttpRouteScope
      Type Parameters:
      T - The type of the target
      Parameters:
      prefixUri - The URI template of the prefix
      locator - Locates the target later, or completes with null for 404
      routesOf - The routes of a located target
